title: [WT-10P] Proxy: preserve bounded blocking replies after one-shot stdin EOF
description:
Objective: make wrapper-issued wait_for_resource usable through the actual one-shot moe-proxy transport before WT-10 relies on it. Verified source defect: scripts/moe-agent.sh moe_rpc and PS Invoke-MoeRpc pipe one request then close stdin; packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts gracefulShutdown uses a flat 2000ms drain, so queued blocking requests are cancelled long before their own timeout. Existing memory mem:gotcha-moe-proxy-oneshot-kills-blocking-longpolls confirms real-daemon reproduction.
Deliverable: bounded EOF-drain handling for known blocking wait_for_resource/wait_for_task/chat_wait requests using their recorded request deadlines. Keep explicit SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown promptly bounded, ordinary-request/empty EOF behavior unchanged, no indefinite reconnect/wait, and deterministic error responses when the request cannot finish. Regression coverage in packages/moe-proxy/src/index.test.ts with the real spawned proxy and fake WS server; inspect existing pendingRequestTimes/getRequestTimeout and shutdown tests before planning. Expected edited files: src/index.ts and src/index.test.ts; avoid wrapper-specific stdin-holding workarounds.
NOT in scope: caller identity, task state, lease semantics, changing daemon tool contracts or installing/restarting the live fleet. WT-10 must use a proxy built from this fix; packaged rollout is owned by epic hardening.
Verification from repo root: (cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test) && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh. Regression tests must spawn compiled current source, not stale dist.
definitionOfDone: A real proxy receiving a known blocking tools/call followed by stdin EOF returns a delayed valid daemon response after more than 2 seconds instead of Proxy shutting down before response received; the test fails on current source.
A blocked request with no daemon response exits within its recorded finite deadline and emits a truthful error; unavailable/disconnected daemon and queued-unsent requests do not hang indefinitely.
SIGINT/SIGTERM remain promptly bounded even while an EOF-drain is pending, and all timeout/connection/process cleanup executes without duplicate responses or leaked children.
Ordinary requests and no-pending-request EOF retain existing shutdown behavior, demonstrated by unchanged existing tests.
The exact verification command exits 0 and the current proxy build is the binary under test.
